sn5.8:0.3: The Discourse about Sīsupacālā Thus I have heard:
sn5.8:1.1: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
sn5.8:1.2: Then the nun Sīsupacālā, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up her bowl and robe, was entering Sāvatthī for alms. After walking for alms in Sāvatthī, and returning from the alms-round after the meal, she approached the Blind Man’s Wood to pass the day, and having entered Blind Man’s Wood,
sn5.8:1.3: she sat down at the root of a certain tree to pass the day.
sn5.8:1.4: Then the Wicked Māra approached the nun Sīsupacālā, and after approaching he said this to the nun Sīsupacālā:
sn5.8:1.5: “Which heresy, nun, are you pleased with?”
sn5.8:1.6: “I am not pleased, friend, with any heresy.”
sn5.8:2.1: “On whose account was your head shaved,
sn5.8:2.2: as you look like an ascetic,
sn5.8:2.4: why (then) do you live like a fool?”
sn5.8:3.1: “Outside of this there are heretics who are stuck fast in their views,
sn5.8:3.3: In their Dhamma I am not pleased,
sn5.8:3.4: their Dhamma is lacking in skill.
sn5.8:4.1: An unmatched Awakened One is born in the Sakya family,
sn5.8:5.3: Attained to the end of all deeds,
sn5.8:5.4: free in the ending of clinging,
sn5.8:5.5: The Fortunate One is my teacher,
sn5.8:5.6: in his Teaching I am well-pleased.”
sn5.8:6.1: Then the Wicked Māra (thought): “The nun Sīsupacālā knows me!” and pained and depressed he vanished right there.
